text: The June jobs report badly missed forecasts at just 57,000 payrolls added while inflation remains elevated at 3.5%, creating a stagflationary setup where the economy is slowing but the Fed may still need to hike — this combination raises the risk of a broader market pullback.

Trim QBTS — this quantum computing stock is down 26% with no earnings to back it up and more than 50% off its high, so reducing your exposure here protects you from further damage in a speculative name with no profit cushion.
Trim IonQ — it's down 18%, nearly 50% off its high, has negative earnings, almost 13% short interest, and insider selling, which all point to reducing your risk in this position before it gets worse.
Raise your EXFY stop from $1.43 to $1.50 to lock in a bit more protection on a stock with mixed technicals and thin profitability.
Raise your MSFT stop from $400.39 to $423.53 to protect more of your gains as the stock has moved higher.

Adobe looks like a strong add opportunity — under 10x earnings with double-digit revenue growth and nearly 10% free cash flow yield (cash profits relative to price) makes it one of the cheapest quality tech names you own.
Consider adding to Meta — 22% revenue growth at under 17x earnings is genuinely cheap for a business this profitable, and the valuation gives you a margin of safety even if markets pull back.
